name: drift-check
summary: Sweep a system in use for divergence from its own intent, classify why each instance happened, and route it to the skill that resolves it.

when: a system has been in use and nobody knows how far it has moved
hardcoded values, local re-implementations or stale versions are suspected
two products that share a system no longer look like they do
not: comparing ONE component against ONE spec

steps: Name the reference point first. Drift is always relative to something, and if there is no single source of truth, THAT is the top finding.
Sweep four dimensions: visual (spacing, colour, radius), behavioural (states, focus, motion), API (prop names and semantics), and token (raw values where a token belongs, or the wrong tier).

Measure it. lint_hardcodes finds raw values, validate_theme_refs finds references to tokens that no longer exist, lint_intent finds a destructive action wearing the primary colour. A drift report assembled by reading is a drift report of what you happened to open.

Classify every instance, because the response depends on WHY: a deliberate documented exception, version lag, accidental divergence, a misreading of the docs, or a gap where the system did not have what was needed.
Weight severity by where it sits. The same drift on a checkout control and on a layout wrapper are not the same finding.

Route each one: an exception becomes a decision record, version lag becomes a migration plan, accidental drift gets fixed AND the doc that failed to prevent it gets reviewed, a misreading is a documentation gap, a system gap is a contribution.
Then step back and name the ROOT PATTERNS. Individual findings get fixed; a root cause stops the next fifty.
output: A findings table with location, dimension, classification, severity and action; then the classification groups; then the root patterns.
done: every finding carries a classification and a named next skill, not just a description
the numbers came from gates that were run, and their output is quoted
system gaps are distinguished from mistakes — a team that worked around a real gap did not do something wrong
the root-pattern section says something the findings list does not
